role: fixed-weight development-derived prompt diagnostic; no training or qualification
limitations: Known development-derived instructions, not final evaluation.
Conditional yes/no scores are not calibrated truth.
Longer prompts can overflow; compare common eligible rows.
The replacement instructions are derived from inspected development errors; this is prompt adaptation with unchanged weights, not learned improvement or untouched final evaluation.
Full-denominator gates treat over-budget rows as rejection. Common-eligible gates separate changed judgments from overflow; longer prompts newly exclude six calibration and three development rows.
Two previously accepted known-failure development candidates are newly over budget. Their exclusion is not evidence of corrected reasoning.

Both prompt sets retain all twelve positive source controls and reject all 24 negative controls under support and joint thresholds; these reused authored interventions do not establish general grounding.
The replacement increases known-failure admissions on both common-eligible splits. Preserve the negative result and existing labels, including entity-typo/metonymy ambiguity.

Failure of this prompt adaptation does not establish a foundation capacity limit; the checkpoint was trained under the original instructions. Future fine-grained training or representation changes require a separate protocol and qualification.

instructions.support: Based only on the supplied evidence, is the proposed answer to the question supported? Answer yes or no.
instructions.completeness: Does the proposed answer supply all the information requested by the question, regardless of whether its factual values are correct? Answer yes or no.
instructions.constraints: Does the proposed answer correctly answer the question while respecting all of its restrictions? Use only the supplied evidence. Answer yes or no.

instructions.support: Using only the supplied evidence, is every factual assertion in the proposed answer supported? Check the exact entities, relationships, categories, quantities and qualifiers. The question is a request, not factual evidence. Do not silently correct names, substitute related categories or transfer a fact from one entity to another. Answer yes only if every assertion is supported; otherwise answer no.
instructions.completeness: Does the proposed answer supply all the information requested by the question, regardless of whether its factual values are correct? Answer yes or no.
instructions.constraints: Using only the supplied evidence, does the proposed answer correctly satisfy every restriction in the question? Treat claims made by the question as unverified unless the evidence establishes them. Check the exact entities, relationships, categories, quantities and qualifiers. Answer yes only if every restriction is satisfied; otherwise answer no.
